github.pr.author: seangeo
github.pr.body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?

Some refactoring to Tracker:

1.  Move the state logic out of Rollcall.Tracker into Rollcall.Tracker.State. 
2. Remove handle_cast, which isn't needed anymore. 
3. Reorder the functions in Tracker. 

No new behaviour, just reorganisation.
github.pr.head: refactor/rollcall-tracker
github.pr.title: refactor(rollcall): extract Tracker.State and reorder Tracker

--- /dev/null
+++ b/rollcall/lib/rollcall/tracker/state.ex
@@ -0,0 +1,146 @@
+defmodule Rollcall.Tracker.State do
+  @moduledoc """
+  The state of a tracker process.
+
+  `local` holds the entries that processes on this node track. `version`
+  counts the changes to `local`. `incarnation` is the monotonic time at which
+  the tracker started. `sent` holds the `local` set and the `version` at the last
+  heartbeat. The struct has no `sent` field yet.
+
+  The `incarnation` and the `version` form the stamp of a message. A peer
+  compares stamps to order messages that arrive in any order. A tracker that
+  restarts gets a newer incarnation, so its peers replace its old entries.
+
+  Monotonic time orders the incarnations of one VM only. A peer keeps one
+  record for each node name, so a node that restarts under a new name gets a
+  new record, and no order between VMs is needed.
+
+  This design assumes that a node restart does not reuse a node name. A new VM
+  that reuses a name can start with a lower incarnation. The peers then treat
+  its messages as stale. A stale message still resets the silent count, so the
+  silence threshold never purges the old record, and the old entries stay, under
+  a very specific time drift that goes backwards during a node restart.
+
+  `peers` maps each peer node to its `Rollcall.Tracker.Peer`. The view of the
+  tracker is `local` plus the replica of each peer. `silence_threshold` is the
+  number of ticks without a message after which the tracker deletes a peer
+  record.
+
+  `monitors` maps each process that has an entry to its monitor. `empty_grace`
+  and `empty_timer` control the stop of a tracker that holds no entry.
+  """
+
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Changes
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Local
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Messages
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Peer
+
+  # `local` has no default. A default runs `Local.new/0` at compile time, and
+  # the struct would then hold a literal value of the opaque type `Local.t()`.
+  @enforce_keys [
+    :scope,
+    :incarnation,
+    :empty_grace,
+    :local,
+    :silence_threshold,
+    :transport_module,
+    :transport_state,
+    :heartbeat_period
+  ]
+
+  defstruct [
+    :scope,
+    :incarnation,
+    :empty_grace,
+    :local,
+    :silence_threshold,
+    :transport_module,
+    :transport_state,
+    :heartbeat_period,
+    empty_timer: nil,
+    version: 0,
+    monitors: %{},
+    peers: %{}
+  ]
+
+  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
+          scope: Rollcall.scope(),
+          incarnation: integer(),
+          empty_grace: non_neg_integer(),
+          empty_timer: reference() | nil,
+          heartbeat_period: pos_integer() | :manual,
+          local: Local.t(),
+          version: non_neg_integer(),
+          monitors: %{pid() => reference()},
+          peers: %{node() => Peer.t()},
+          silence_threshold: pos_integer(),
+          transport_module: module(),
+          transport_state: any()
+        }
+
+  @doc """
+  Sets `local`. The version increases by one when `changes` is not empty.
+  """
+  @spec apply_changes(t(), Local.t(), Changes.t()) :: t()
+  def apply_changes(%__MODULE__{} = state, local, changes) do
+    state = %{state | local: local}
+
+    if Changes.empty?(changes) do
+      state
+    else
+      bump_version(state)
+    end
+  end
+
+  @spec bump_version(t()) :: t()
+  defp bump_version(%__MODULE__{version: version} = state) do
+    %{state | version: version + 1}
+  end
+
+  @spec current_stamp(t()) :: Messages.stamp()
+  def current_stamp(%__MODULE__{incarnation: incarnation, version: version}) do
+    Messages.stamp(incarnation, version)
+  end
+
+  @inspectable_keys [:incarnation, :scope, :version, :local, :peers]
+
+  @typedoc "The fields of the state that have a meaning outside the process."
+  @type view :: %{
+          scope: Rollcall.scope(),
+          version: non_neg_integer(),
+          incarnation: integer(),
+          local: Local.t(),
+          peers: %{node() => Peer.t()}
+        }
+
+  @doc """
+  Returns the fields of the state that have a meaning outside the process.
+
+  The timer, the monitors and the transport stay private, so a change to them
+  does not break a caller.
+  """
+  @spec inspect_view(t()) :: view()
+  def inspect_view(%__MODULE__{} = state) do
+    Map.take(state, @inspectable_keys)
+  end
+
+  @doc "Returns the record of the peer on `node`, or `nil` when no message came from that node."
+  @spec peer(t(), node()) :: Peer.t() | nil
+  def peer(%__MODULE__{peers: peers}, node) do
+    Map.get(peers, node)
+  end
+
+  @doc "Sets the record of the peer on `node`."
+  @spec put_peer(t(), node(), Peer.t()) :: t()
+  def put_peer(%__MODULE__{peers: peers} = state, node, %Peer{} = peer) do
+    %{state | peers: Map.put(peers, node, peer)}
+  end
+
+  @doc """
+  Returns the stamp of the goodbye: the incarnation and the version plus one.
+  """
+  @spec goodbye_stamp(t()) :: Messages.stamp()
+  def goodbye_stamp(%__MODULE__{incarnation: incarnation, version: version}) do
+    Messages.stamp(incarnation, version + 1)
+  end
+end

@@ -0,0 +1,143 @@
+defmodule Rollcall.Tracker.StateTest do
+  use ExUnit.Case, async: true
+
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Changes
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Entry
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Local
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.Peer
+  alias Rollcall.Tracker.State
+
+  @incarnation 1_000
+
+  setup do
+    state = %State{
+      scope: "scope",
+      incarnation: @incarnation,
+      empty_grace: 5_000,
+      local: Local.new(),
+      silence_threshold: 10,
+      heartbeat_period: :manual,
+      transport_module: Rollcall.Transport.Null,
+      transport_state: nil
+    }
+
+    %{state: state}
+  end
+
+  describe "apply_changes/3" do
+    test "sets local and increases the version when the changes are not empty", %{state: state} do
+      {changes, local} = Local.track(state.local, self(), "partition", "key", %{}, make_ref())
+
+      state = State.apply_changes(state, local, changes)
+
+      assert state.local == local
+      assert state.version == 1
+    end
+
+    test "increases the version by one for each change", %{state: state} do
+      {changes_1, local_1} = Local.track(state.local, self(), "partition", "key_1", %{}, make_ref())
+      {changes_2, local_2} = Local.track(local_1, self(), "partition", "key_2", %{}, make_ref())
+
+      state =
+        state
+        |> State.apply_changes(local_1, changes_1)
+        |> State.apply_changes(local_2, changes_2)
+
+      assert state.version == 2
+    end
+
+    test "sets local and keeps the version when the changes are empty", %{state: state} do
+      {_changes, local} = Local.track(state.local, self(), "partition", "key", %{}, make_ref())
+
+      state = State.apply_changes(state, local, Changes.new())
+
+      assert state.local == local
+      assert state.version == 0
+    end
+
+    test "counts a change that only has leaves", %{state: state} do
+      entry = Entry.new(self(), "partition", "key", %{}, make_ref())
+
+      state = State.apply_changes(state, state.local, Changes.new([], [entry]))
+
+      assert state.version == 1
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "peer/2 and put_peer/3" do
+    test "peer/2 returns nil for a node that sent no message", %{state: state} do
+      assert State.peer(state, :a@host) == nil
+    end
+
+    test "peer/2 returns the record that put_peer/3 set", %{state: state} do
+      peer = %Peer{silent_ticks: 2}
+
+      state = State.put_peer(state, :a@host, peer)
+
+      assert State.peer(state, :a@host) == peer
+    end
+
+    test "put_peer/3 replaces the record of the node", %{state: state} do
+      state =
+        state
+        |> State.put_peer(:a@host, %Peer{silent_ticks: 2})
+        |> State.put_peer(:a@host, %Peer{silent_ticks: 0})
+
+      assert State.peer(state, :a@host) == %Peer{silent_ticks: 0}
+    end
+
+    test "put_peer/3 keeps the records of the other nodes", %{state: state} do
+      state =
+        state
+        |> State.put_peer(:a@host, %Peer{silent_ticks: 1})
+        |> State.put_peer(:b@host, %Peer{silent_ticks: 2})
+
+      assert State.peer(state, :a@host) == %Peer{silent_ticks: 1}
+      assert State.peer(state, :b@host) == %Peer{silent_ticks: 2}
+    end
+
+    test "put_peer/3 does not change the other fields", %{state: state} do
+      assert %{State.put_peer(state, :a@host, %Peer{}) | peers: %{}} == state
+    end
+  end
+
+  describe "inspect_view/1" do
+    test "returns the fields that have a meaning outside the process", %{state: state} do
+      peer = %Peer{silent_ticks: 2}
+      state = %{state | version: 3} |> State.put_peer(:a@host, peer)
+
+      assert State.inspect_view(state) == %{
+               scope: "scope",
+               version: 3,
+               incarnation: @incarnation,
+               local: state.local,
+               peers: %{a@host: peer}
+             }
+    end
+
+    test "leaves out the timer, the monitors and the transport", %{state: state} do
+      view = State.inspect_view(state)
+
+      refute Map.has_key?(view, :empty_timer)

+defmodule Rollcall.Transport.PassThrough do
+  @moduledoc """
+  A transport for tests that need to choose the origin of each message.
+
+  A test sends `{:deliver, scope, message}` to the tracker. `unwrap/2` returns
+  the scope and the message as they are, so the origin stays the pid that the
+  test chose. `Rollcall.Transport.InMemory` rewrites the origin.
+
+  The tracker sends no message through this transport.
+  """
+
+  @behaviour Rollcall.Transport
+
+  @impl true
+  def init(scope, _opts), do: {:ok, scope}
+
+  @impl true
+  def heartbeat(_scope, _message), do: :ok
+
+  @impl true
+  def unwrap(_scope, {:deliver, scope, message}), do: {:ok, scope, message}
+  def unwrap(_scope, _raw), do: :ignore
+end

+  The tracker uses `Rollcall.Transport.PassThrough`. A test delivers a message
+  with `send(tracker, {:deliver, scope, message})`.
+
   This function is the only place that passes the init parameter.
   """
   @spec start_tracker(Rollcall.scope(), pos_integer()) :: pid()
   def start_tracker(scope, silence_threshold) do
